newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African Bank hikes T-Bill tender by 200 mln rand.
newsitem.headline: S.African Bank hikes T-Bill tender by 200 mln rand.

text.p: The Reserve Bank said on Friday it had increased the amount on offer in its three- and six-month Treasury bills weekly tender by 200 million rand in line with government's financing plans for the year.

The central bank said it had invited tenders for 800 million rand of 91-day Treasury bills and 300 million rand 182-day bills on Friday compared with 700 million rand and 200 million rand respectively last week.
Money market traders said the reason for the increase in the tender was linked to recent strong demand for liquid assets.
But Roelf du Plooy, assistant general manager of the Reserve Bank's money and capital markets division, said the higher tender was purely in line with government's budget plans for the year.
"It has been increased in line with what the Minister of Finance budgeted for," Roelf du Plooy told Reuters.
In his 1997/98 budget, Finance Minister Trevor Manuel made provision for government to raise a net two billion rand in Treasury bills.
"It was budgeted for that we would increase the Treasury Bills around this time of the year...and we will increase it at a later stage again," du Plooy said.
Money market traders said the result of the increased tender would result in a slight drop in liquidity in the money market, while the Treasury Bill rate could also tick slightly higher.
"By doing it it will have a slight impact on the liquidity situation...might squeeze the rate up a couple of points, but I don't see much in it," said one trader.
"One would expect that if there is an increase in supply that the price will come down a bit and the rate will go up a bit. Personally I expect the rate to increase a little bit," du Plooy said.
The 91-day T-bill rate stood at 15.69 percent last week, while the six-month rate stood at 15.20 percent. The results of this week's tender will be announced at 1000 GMT.
Du Plooy added that the reason for the money market shortage's rise back above the nine billion rand mark was a result of increased notes and coins in circulation ahead of Thursday's market holiday.
The shortage stood at 9.169 billion rand on Wednesday from 8.935 billion rand before, while notes and coins increased to 21.222 billion rand from 20.696 billion rand on Tuesday.
Major banks kept their three month deposit rates steady at between 16.40 to 16.45 percent offered, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at between 15.80 to 15.95 percent.
